title: Wing Lower Cover Panel — Scarfed Composite Patch Repair

ata.title: Wing Box Structure — Lower Cover Panels

abstract: Scarfed composite patch repair for impact damage and delamination in the wing lower cover panel, restoring full static strength where the damage stays inside the drawing envelope.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static strength and the stiffness of the wing lower cover panel after impact damage or delamination, using a scarfed and co-bonded composite patch.
sections.damage_assessment: Map the damage by ultrasonic inspection over an area of at least 300 mm around the visible impact, because the delamination footprint is always larger than the surface mark. This repair is valid where the delaminated area is no larger than 120 mm across, where no more than four plies are affected and where the damage does not reach a fastener row, a rib foot or the spanwise splice. Damage that reaches the splice, damage through more than four plies, and any damage with fibre breakage on the inner surface are outside the scope of this repair. Record the ply orientation at the damage site from the panel layup table before any material is removed.
sections.repair_procedure: Dry the panel to the schedule in the standard practice before any material is removed; a wet laminate will not bond. Machine the scarf to the ratio given on the repair drawing, working ply by ply and recording each ply as it is removed. Clean the scarf and do a solvent wipe with the approved agent. Lay up the replacement plies in the same orientation as the removed plies, with the additional cover ply shown on the drawing. Apply the vacuum bag and cure to the schedule on the drawing, keeping the thermocouples on the positions shown. Do an ultrasonic inspection of the cured patch and of the surrounding parent laminate. Where the repair boundary reaches the stiffener D5710123576997 or the splice strap INN928999-53, stop and get an engineering assessment before continuing. Prepare the perimeter holes for the lightning mesh tab to the clearance fit given on sheet 3, ream them to the stated finish and install the blind rivets AGS769415-6A. Restore the lightning protection mesh and the surface finish, and check the electrical bonding resistance across the repair.
sections.inspection_requirements: A repair inside the drawing envelope carries no life limit but needs an ultrasonic inspection of the patch and its boundary at every six-year check. Check the electrical bonding resistance at the same interval. A repair that shows any growth of the ultrasonic indication must be reported to Aeralis immediately and the aircraft must not be dispatched until an assessment is received. Record the cure trace with the repair paperwork; a repair without a cure trace is not acceptable.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Delamination up to 120 mm across affecting no more than four plies, clear of any fastener row, rib foot or spanwise splice, with no fibre breakage on the inner surface.

repair_drawings.title: Scarfed composite patch, wing lower cover panel

type_data.fastener_pattern: Not applicable, bonded repair. Fasteners are used only to hold the lightning mesh tab.
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit inside the drawing envelope. Ultrasonic inspection of the patch and its boundary at every six-year check, with an electrical bonding check at the same interval.

ata.title: Wing Box Structure — Lower Cover Panels

abstract: Scarfed composite patch repair for impact damage and delamination in the wing lower cover panel, in two variants by fastener standard, restoring full static strength where the damage stays inside the drawing envelope.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static strength and the stiffness of the wing lower cover panel after impact damage or delamination, using a scarfed and co-bonded composite patch. Two variants of the perimeter attachment are published, one for the clearance-fit fastener standard and one for the cold-worked interference-fit standard; the laminate work is common to both.
sections.damage_assessment: Map the damage by ultrasonic inspection over an area of at least 300 mm around the visible impact, because the delamination footprint is always larger than the surface mark. This repair is valid where the delaminated area is no larger than 120 mm across, where no more than four plies are affected and where the damage does not reach a fastener row, a rib foot or the spanwise splice. Damage that reaches the splice, damage through more than four plies, and any damage with fibre breakage on the inner surface are outside the scope of this repair. Record the ply orientation at the damage site from the panel layup table before any material is removed.
sections.repair_procedure: Dry the panel to the schedule in the standard practice before any material is removed; a wet laminate will not bond. Machine the scarf to the ratio given on the repair drawing, working ply by ply and recording each ply as it is removed. Clean the scarf and do a solvent wipe with the approved agent. Lay up the replacement plies in the same orientation as the removed plies, with the additional cover ply shown on the drawing. Apply the vacuum bag and cure to the schedule on the drawing, keeping the thermocouples on the positions shown. Do an ultrasonic inspection of the cured patch and of the surrounding parent laminate. Where the repair boundary reaches the stiffener D5710123576997 or the splice strap INN928999-53, stop and get an engineering assessment before continuing. Then prepare the perimeter attachment to the variant that matches the panel. Variant 1, pre MOD-161688: drill and ream the perimeter holes to the clearance fit on sheet 3 and install the blind rivets AGS769415-6A. Variant 2, post MOD-161688: the panel is cold worked for the interference-fit fastener AGS17834-4B and the clearance bore of variant 1 must not be used. Driving the interference fastener into a clearance-prepared hole crushes the laminate at the hole wall; opening the bore to clear it leaves the joint under-clamped. Prepare the holes with the mandrel and the reamer sizes on sheet 4, check each bore with the plug gauge before installation and install the fastener to the stated interference. Restore the lightning protection mesh and the surface finish, and check the electrical bonding resistance across the repair.
sections.inspection_requirements: A repair inside the drawing envelope carries no life limit but needs an ultrasonic inspection of the patch and its boundary at every six-year check. Check the electrical bonding resistance at the same interval; the interference-fit perimeter of variant 2 gives a lower initial bonding resistance and the acceptance figure on sheet 4 is the one to read for it. A repair that shows any growth of the ultrasonic indication must be reported to Aeralis immediately and the aircraft must not be dispatched until an assessment is received. Record the cure trace and the variant used with the repair paperwork; a repair without a cure trace is not acceptable.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Delamination up to 120 mm across affecting no more than four plies, clear of any fastener row, rib foot or spanwise splice, with no fibre breakage on the inner surface.

repair_drawings.title: Scarfed composite patch, wing lower cover panel, clearance-fit and interference-fit perimeter variants

type_data.fastener_pattern: Not applicable, bonded repair. Fasteners are used only to hold the lightning mesh tab: clearance fit in variant 1, cold-worked interference fit in variant 2.
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit inside the drawing envelope. Ultrasonic inspection of the patch and its boundary at every six-year check, with an electrical bonding check at the same interval.
